title: Molecular speeds in a gas
hook: Change absolute temperature and predict root-mean-square molecular speed.
misconception: root-mean-square molecular speed doubles when absolute temperature doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v_rms = √(3kT/m) to compare root-mean-square molecular speed when absolute temperature changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal gas with fixed molecular mass, v_rms = √(3kT/m). When absolute temperature doubles, root-mean-square molecular speed becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v_rms = √(3kT/m); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal gas with fixed molecular mass, with a nonzero initial result. If absolute temperature triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on root-mean-square molecular speed?
recall.why: Apply v_rms = √(3kT/m) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
